clue.text: To lead on is wrong, leading to great distress

indicators.note: the letters of to lead on are wrong, i.e. set out in a wrong order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone warns that stringing a person along is wrong and ends in misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' rearranges the ten letters of TO LEAD ON; 'leading to' is only the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolation is a state of utter misery and grief, the same as great distress.

clue.text: Call for more directions to the centre

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
N is north, a compass direction
the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A request for more instructions on how to get downtown.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an audience's shout for a performer to give an extra piece.

clue.text: Proposal to provide public with running water

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A plan to supply the population with piped water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an approach or offer made to open negotiations.

clue.text: Breaking off a story people make up

parts.note: a lie is a story, a made-up tale
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Ending a relationship over a tale that people have invented.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is estrangement, the breaking off of friendly relations.

clue.text: Tearing madly about for an unappreciative individual

indicators.note: the letters of tearing are thrown madly about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rushing wildly around for an ungrateful person.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is a person who shows no gratitude.

clue.text: The head may be under water

definitions.text: The head may be under water

parts.words: The head may be under water
parts.note: a headland or promontory, which a high tide or flood might cover; also the famous Scottish loch

explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a headland or cape, a point of land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Drinks will be provided for the men on board

definitions.meaning: the pieces used in a board game played on a chequered board

explanation.definitionFit: Draughts are long drinks, and also the British name for checkers, whose pieces are men.

clue.text: Outraged, though that may be dead secret

indicators.note: the letters of dead secret may be rearranged to form another word

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked, though the matter may be kept quiet for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals that DEAD SECRET is rearranged; 'though that' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: To desecrate a holy place is to violate or outrage it, so desecrated means outraged.

clue.text: An admission of course

definitions.meaning: the right or privilege of being admitted somewhere
a dish served as one stage of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to something, as one naturally would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as the idiom 'naturally'; split it and 'course' is a stage of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means both the right of entry to a place and a dish served at dinner.

clue.text: Turn informer about the company that's found to be twisting

indicators.note: the informer's word goes round, sitting about the company word

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
a crew is a company, e.g. a ship's company

explanation.surface: A gang member turns informer on his firm, which is shown to be crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwing is turning something round on its thread, i.e. twisting it.

clue.text: Concerned with the way a foreign priest provides therapy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman from abroad offers a kind of treatment for those worried about the path they are on.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a treatment consisting of a long period of rest, so a form of therapy.

clue.text: Fare offered in some nurseries

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the words some nurseries

explanation.surface: A list of food served in certain children's nurseries.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is the list of dishes a restaurant has on offer.

clue.text: Mark one turning up at the last minute for work

parts.note: to mark an opponent in team sports is to man-mark him, so mark gives man
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word up is turned over, read the other way

parts.note: late means at the last minute

explanation.surface: A man arrives just in time for his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses UP to PU, which follows I. MARK for MAN is loose; it may be the sporting sense of marking (manning) an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To work something is to handle or operate it skilfully, i.e. manipulate it.

clue.text: A number to irritate a woman? Quite!

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written
to get someone is to annoy them, as in it really gets me
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a song is meant to annoy a lady, and is answered emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like a song; it is A plus the Roman numeral L.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is an emphatic word meaning entirely or completely, as an exclaimed quite! does.

clue.text: "For forms of let fools contest."(Pope)

parts.note: a missing word from Pope's Essay on Man, 'For forms of ___ let fools contest; whate'er is best administer'd is best'

explanation.definitionFit: The quotation from Alexander Pope's Essay on Man argues that the form of rule matters less than how well it is run.

clue.text: Vengeance, making sin seem awful

indicators.note: the words sin seem are made awful, i.e. mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Retribution makes wrongdoing look dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, and the word now means just punishment or revenge.

clue.text: This offers potential savers an opening

definitions.text: This offers potential savers an opening

parts.words: This offers potential savers an opening
parts.note: a container with a slot into which thrifty people drop coins

explanation.definitionFit: A money box is a small container with a slot for keeping savings.

clue.text: Disturbed by a few lines in the Old Testament

indicators.note: the lines are put in the Testament abbreviation

parts.note: OT is the standard abbreviation for the Old Testament
a verse is a few lines of poetry or scripture

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a passage of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Overset is an old word for upset or overturned, so disturbed.

clue.text: Genuine acceptance of publicity is giving satisfaction

indicators.note: the genuine word accepts, i.e. takes in, the following letters

parts.note: real means genuine
PR is public relations, publicity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Real, accepted publicity is pleasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is retaliation, taking satisfaction for an injury, as in demanding satisfaction.

clue.text: After midnight youngsters sparkle

indicators.note: the youngsters come after the midnight letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G
a litter is a brood of young animals

explanation.surface: Children twinkle after the clock strikes twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the middle of 'night', the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter is to shine with bright flashes of light, i.e. to sparkle.

clue.text: American beggar — a kitchen worker?

definitions.meaning: in the US a beggar who accosts people in the street
jokingly, someone who handles the pots and pans

explanation.definitionFit: The US term for a street beggar, playfully read as someone who handles saucepans.

clue.text: Prompt and quiet staff

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a rod is a stick or staff

explanation.surface: A request for a swift, silent walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod someone is to urge or nudge them into action, i.e. prompt them.

clue.text: Big bloomer made by a revered figure in ancient Egypt

definitions.text: a revered figure in ancient Egypt

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very big
an iris is a flower, a bloomer

explanation.surface: A big blunder made by a respected Egyptian worthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a blunder; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and the afterlife, worshipped in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Non-professional dealing with an idler

parts.note: lay means amateur, not of a profession
about means concerning or dealing with

explanation.surface: An amateur is faced with someone lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is a lazy person who avoids work, i.e. an idler.

clue.text: A Scandinavian writing of taking in the French

indicators.note: the word of takes in, encloses, the French article

parts.note: taken as written
la is French for the

explanation.surface: A Norseman writes about bringing in French people.
explanation.definitionFit: Olaf is a common Scandinavian man's name, borne by several Norwegian kings.

clue.text: Esteem rate reform certain

indicators.note: the word rate is reformed, its letters put into a new order

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A headline-like demand that rates be overhauled with confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure someone is to value them highly, i.e. hold them in esteem.

clue.text: A Russian vehicle with ample horse-power!

definitions.text: A Russian vehicle with ample horse-power!

parts.words: A Russian vehicle with ample horse-power!
parts.note: a Russian carriage pulled by three horses abreast, so plenty of literal horse-power

explanation.surface: A Russian car with a powerful engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage drawn by a team of three horses.

clue.text: Tops for those starting school

definitions.meaning: pupils in their first year of school, the first form

explanation.definitionFit: First-class means of the highest quality, and a first class is the youngest group at school.
